questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle takes longer to stop, leave more space between you and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume it handles the same as your own bike.
Trust that the owner checked the brakes.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles so you have more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles so you have more time to react.
questions.explanation: Check the motorcycle the same way you would check your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and leave extra space for stopping.

questions.question: When should you keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to enjoy the view.
To encourage other drivers to cut in front of you.
To hide from the driver ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when conditions make stopping difficult. This includes slippery roads, limited visibility, and heavy traffic where another vehicle might cut in front of you.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If it is safe, change lanes and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up may only make things worse by encouraging them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch out for oily areas, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges because they have less traction.

questions.question: How should you position your feet when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down as they might catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: What is the rule when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within speed limits and only where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: Where should you ride when following a car?

options.text: In the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position helps them see you.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: How do you make the shortest and safest stop?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes in a smooth, gradual way without skidding either tire. This gives you the shortest and safest stop.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation standards.
questions.explanation: Buy a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly around your head and have no visible damage.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up, not to steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Press your knees against the gas tank while riding to help balance during turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Tell your passenger not to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat made for two riders to carry a passenger. It must also have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same safety gear that you wear.

questions.question: What is the main active chemical in marijuana?
questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: The main active chemical in marijuana is called tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of these, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip.
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know the location of all controls before you ride.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends the SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, Execute
questions.explanation: Safe riders use the SEE strategy: Search, Evaluate, and Execute. This helps you make good decisions while riding.

questions.question: Night riding is safer when you:

options.text: Know that other drivers cannot see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, stop and rest every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. When the system detects a wheel about to lock, it releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep the wheel rolling and maintain stopping power.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while you ride.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely for protection. Your clothing should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection if you have an accident.

questions.question: You can increase your visibility by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can increase visibility by wearing bright clothing or reflective materials. Adding extra lights to your motorcycle, using turn signals, and flashing your brake light help other drivers see you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Have a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Have a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
Have a sudden loss of power to the front wheel.
Have a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a sudden loss of power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to escape a slippery road.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check your blind spots as part of your regular scanning routine.
